source.title: Symbolic Discovery of Optimization Algorithms
source.authors: Xiangning Chen; Chen Liang; Da Huang; E. Real; Kai-Yuan Wang; Yao Liu; Hieu Pham; Xuanyi Dong; Thang Luong; Cho-Jui Hsieh; Yifeng Lu; Quoc V. Le

page_placements.theme: Optimizer design and tuning affect held-out rankings

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no evident truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizers on held-out performance and reports training error and a loss-perturbation measure; it does not directly test the random-label, architecture, or magnitude-aware sharpness versions.
record.gate_note: Lion versus AdamW/Adafactor comparisons bear on optimizer-dependent generalization (V4). The study also varies batch size at a fixed epoch budget (V5). It does not report random-label memorization, width sweeps, convolution-versus-fully-connected comparisons, dropout effects, or removal of memorized examples. Other optimizer benchmark scores are not included here where they do not add a distinct claim-relevant result.
record.test_reason: The fixed-300-epoch batch-size sweep tests V5 in a new ViT/ImageNet setting. Table 2 also compares AdamW with momentum SGD on ResNet-50, bearing on V4 under learning-rate and weight-decay tuning. Lion-versus-AdamW results alone do not test adaptive methods versus SGD.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that program search discovers a memory-efficient optimizer that transfers across tasks. Lion often improves performance over AdamW or Adafactor, but gains depend on task, architecture, augmentation and batch size, and some differences are small or not statistically significant. Performance below batch size 64 is a tentative limitation, not a demonstrated threshold.
record.recipe_differences: Compares a newly discovered optimizer, Lion, against AdamW and other optimizers on benchmark training tasks; does not reproduce the original studies' interventions or measures. Relevant comparisons tune peak learning rate and decoupled weight decay.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer and batch size; authors also report that Lion's advantage decreases with strong augmentations and is small or absent on some tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Lion has higher unperturbed training loss but lower loss under Gaussian weight perturbations than AdamW: 0.75 versus 0.61, and 1.37 versus 3.74.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this ViT-B/16 ImageNet setting, Lion tolerates the authors' unscaled Gaussian weight perturbations better than AdamW.

fits_no_version.finding: Lion exceeds AdamW in ImageNet accuracy by 0.65 percentage points for augmented ViT-B/16 and 0.11 points for ResNet-50.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lion can improve held-out image-classification accuracy over AdamW, with gains depending on architecture and training conditions.

record.problems: The relevant optimizer results do not directly report the training-to-test gap for most settings; only the ViT-B/16 appendix table gives training error, and the flatness measure is not magnitude-aware sharpness. Batch-size accuracy comparisons are reported in text for 32K; other batch-size values are figure-based. The study does not report uncertainty for the individual benchmark scores in the extracted rows.
record.rows_left_out: Other optimizer and task comparisons in Tables 1–7 and 10–12, and Figures 1, 4–7, 9–12, were left out because they report benchmark performance without a distinct direct result on the mapped optimizer or batch-size conditions, or provide repeated task-specific optimizer comparisons beyond the selected rows. No random-label, width-sweep, architecture-family, dropout, or memorized-example-removal results are reported.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding natural-label and random-label held-out accuracies.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Controlled convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparisons and learned or transferred local connectivity.

The limited-learning-rate/schedule-tuning regime, matched training performance for adaptive methods versus SGD, switching to SGD, and adaptive-versus-SGD language-model comparisons. The direct numerical SGD comparison is limited to ResNet-50.
Language-model batch sweeps, longer-training remedies, and controlled tests of warmup, normalization, or regularization changes as remedies.
Controlled dropout addition/removal and its dependence on data size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, correlation with generalization gaps across comparable networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

missing.what: A direct V4 comparison row for ResNet-50: momentum SGD 76.22%, AdamW 76.34% ImageNet accuracy, averaged over three runs, 90 epochs, batch 1,024, without RandAug or Mixup. Although Table 2 is broadly mentioned in rows_left_out, this SGD comparison was not identified there as an omitted claim-relevant result.
Within-optimizer smaller-batch accuracy baselines for R4: batch 4,096 gives AdamW 80.12% and Lion 80.77%, versus 75.4% and 77.9% at 32K, under the same 300-epoch augmented ViT-B/16 setup.
missing.locator: Tables 2 and 7; Sections 4.1 and 4.6; Figure 8 left

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. The record's V4 labels improperly substitute Lion for SGD. Its V5 labels improperly treat a between-optimizer comparison and selected optimal batch sizes as direct evidence of a batch penalty. Table 10's paired validation accuracies are 75.48/77.44, not R3's augmented 80.12/80.77.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.

Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD across the image and language benchmarks named in the version, or test limited versus broader tuning. The relevant comparisons here are Lion against AdamW/Adafactor, with learning rate and weight decay tuned.
The reported batch-size sweep is for ViT-B/16 on ImageNet with RandAug and Mixup; it does not test language models or normalization changes.
Dropout addition/removal and its interaction with training set size and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbations and comparison against norm- and margin-based generalization measures.
Removing the most memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Trained with AdamW; reported training error and landscape flatness at convergence.
rows.measure: Training error Ltrain; perturbed training loss LNtrain (average over 1K Gaussian noises).
rows.note: Training error and perturbed training loss are reported, but this row does not itself give held-out performance.
rows.check: Training loss and loss under unscaled Gaussian weight perturbations do not establish V4 or V7. Split these distinct measures. Table 10 concerns the unaugmented setting with AdamW/Lion validation accuracies 75.48/77.44; the extracted augmentation value '7' is a misread symbol.

rows.subject: ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Lion; reported training error and landscape flatness at convergence.
rows.measure: Training error Ltrain; perturbed training loss LNtrain (average over 1K Gaussian noises).
rows.note: Authors state Lion has higher training error but retains comparably lower error against Gaussian perturbations; the latter is a flatness measure, not the magnitude-aware sharpness in V7.
rows.check: Lion versus AdamW does not supply V4's SGD comparison. The perturbation measure lacks V7's magnitude scaling and measure-ranking analysis. Split training loss from perturbed loss; this is the unaugmented Table 10 setting.

rows.subject: ViT-B/16
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Lion; reported ImageNet validation accuracy.
rows.note: Table 2 reports accuracy; this is held-out performance, not a direct numerical training-to-test gap.
rows.check: The 80.12/80.77 accuracies are correct for ViT-B/16 with RandAug and Mixup, but compare Lion with AdamW rather than SGD. This condition is different from R1–R2, so these rows cannot substantiate a joint training-loss/validation-accuracy comparison.

source_check.correct: With RandAug and Mixup, AdamW accuracy is 80.12% and Lion accuracy is 80.77%. Without these augmentations, the corresponding accuracies are 75.48% and 77.44%. The reported values belong to the augmented condition, marked 3 rather than 7 in the extracted table.
source_check.locator_found: Table 2, ViT-B/16 trained from scratch; Table 7; Table 12, augmentation settings.
source_check.problem: Both accuracy values belong to the augmented condition, whereas the row copies the table marker for the unaugmented condition.

rows.subject: ViT-B/16
rows.stage_stated: Train from scratch on ImageNet, 300 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Varied batch size while maintaining total training epochs; compared Lion and AdamW.
rows.note: The paper explicitly reports the large-batch comparison at fixed total epoch count.
rows.check: The reported 32K accuracies are correct, but Lion versus AdamW at one batch size does not itself establish a batch penalty. Add within-optimizer baselines: at batch 4,096 and 300 epochs with augmentation, AdamW achieves 80.12% and Lion 80.77%; at 32K these fall to 75.4% and 77.9%, respectively.

source_check.correct: The recorded cross-optimizer comparison alone has state cannot_determine for V5. Add within-optimizer comparisons at 300 epochs: AdamW accuracy decreases from 80.12% at batch 4,096 to 75.4% at 32K; Lion decreases from 80.77% to 77.9%. These comparisons support state observed.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.6, Effect of batch size; Section 4.1, training duration and default batch size; Table 2, augmented ViT-B/16.
source_check.problem: Lion versus AdamW at one batch size does not establish the within-optimizer batch-size penalty required by V5.

rows.subject: ViT-B/16
rows.stage_stated: Train from scratch on ImageNet, 300 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Varied batch size while maintaining total training epochs; reported the preferred batch size for each optimizer.
rows.measure: Batch size at which the optimizer's accuracy is optimal
rows.locator: Section 4.6, Effect of batch size; Figure 8 (Left)
rows.note: The stated optima show the outcome depends on optimizer; the figure also reports robustness at batch size 64 without a precise accuracy in text.
rows.check: These are selected optimal batch sizes, not held-out performance measurements. Remove as an outcome row and retain as context for the batch-size sweep.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.stage_stated: Train from scratch on ImageNet, 90 epochs
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Lion; compared with AdamW on ImageNet validation accuracy.
rows.uncertainty: Results averaged from three runs; no error bars stated.
rows.note: The accuracy difference is small; authors describe optimizer discrepancies on ResNets as pretty small.
rows.check: The Lion/AdamW values are correct, but their difference does not test V4. Add a separate AdamW-versus-SGD comparison from the same table: 76.34% versus 76.22%. ResNet-50 uses no RandAug or Mixup; Table 2 results are averaged over three runs.
